title: Graph change-notification lifetimes and latency
finding: Webhook subscriptions expire and must be renewed; lifecycle notifications warn of missed events. driveItem average latency <1 min but max 6 hours.
numbers: driveItem sub max 42,300 min (<30 d); Outlook message 10,080 min (<7 d), 1,440 min with resource data; chatMessage 4,320 min (3 d); min 45 min; driveItem max latency 6 h
decision: Never rely on webhooks alone: run a renewal job plus a polling backstop sized to the max delivery latency.

title: Graph delta query: tokens, replays, 410, tombstones
finding: Delta is pull; webhooks are push; combine them. Delta tokens expire, can replay changes, and 410 Gone forces full resync. Deletions arrive as @removed with reason.
numbers: Directory delta token valid 7 days; Outlook token lifetime depends on cache size; 410 Gone => full sync
decision: Treat delta cursor as a lease: idempotent upserts, handle @removed as tombstone, auto-trigger full resync on 410/syncStateNotFound.

title: Google Drive changes feed and push channels
finding: Push notifications carry no content: they only signal that changes.list should be called. Channels do not auto-renew.
numbers: changes channel max 604,800 s (1 wk); files channel max 86,400 s (1 d); default 3,600 s; notification body empty
decision: Webhook = doorbell only. Store startPageToken per user/drive; renew channels with overlap before expiry.

title: Google Drive changes.list page tokens
finding: Cursor pattern: getStartPageToken, then changes.list pages until newStartPageToken; includeRemoved controls removed items.
numbers: Order: oldest first; token persisted after last page
decision: Persist cursor only after the page batch commits (at-least-once, idempotent apply).

title: GitHub webhook delivery contract
finding: Must answer 2xx within a short window; process via queue; redelivery reuses X-GitHub-Delivery so it is a natural dedupe key.
decision: Webhook receiver only validates, enqueues, acks; dedupe on delivery ID; reconcile by periodic list to catch lost events.

title: Jira Cloud points-based rate limits
finding: Hourly point quotas plus per-second burst caps; 429 with Retry-After; quota overrun blocks until the next UTC hour.
numbers: Global pool 65,000 points/h; Standard tenant 100,000+10xusers (cap 500,000)/h; GET burst 100 rps; enforcement from 2026-03-02; identity reads cost 2 points/object
decision: Budget per tenant per connector; backfill must be paced to a share (estimate: <=50%) of the hourly quota so live sync is never starved.

title: Slack API limits and ToS tightening for non-Marketplace apps
finding: Bulk history reads are throttled hard for unlisted commercial apps and ToS restricts storing and sharing data from Slack APIs.
numbers: conversations.history: 1 req/min and 15 objects/page (non-Marketplace); internal custom apps 50+/min, 1,000 objects; ToS effective 2025-05-29 (new) / 2025-06-30 (old apps)
decision: Do not plan a bulk Slack copy as the core design. Prefer Marketplace/internal app status and live query for Slack; check legal terms before storing text.

title: Notion API request limits
finding: Average per-connection limit plus a per-workspace limit shared across connections; 429 with Retry-After.
numbers: Average 3 requests/s per connection (workspace limit scales with plan)
decision: Backfill of large Notion workspaces is slow by design: use webhooks/incremental search and a token bucket per workspace.

title: Rate-limit window guidance for sync engines
finding: Short per-second/minute windows recover fast; hours-long windows can leave data unsynced for the rest of the window once credits run out.
decision: Implement adaptive throttling and reserve a slice of every long-window quota for freshness traffic.

title: Resumable agent/workflow state
finding: Restarting from scratch on failure was too costly; they built resume-from-checkpoint with retries and regular checkpoints.
decision: Run connector syncs as durable, checkpointed workflows (resume at last cursor) rather than long-lived scripts.

title: Dropbox Dash chose index over federated
finding: Index-based retrieval needs heavy infrastructure but beats federated retrieval, which is limited by external APIs, cannot reach company-wide content and inflates tokens.
numbers: Context cap ~100,000 tokens; simple MCP query up to 45 s vs seconds for the raw index
decision: Primary path = own index; live MCP/federated only for fresh or sensitive slices.

title: Microsoft Copilot: synced vs federated connectors
finding: Two modes from one vendor: synced connectors index items (content, metadata, ACL); federated connectors fetch live via MCP with no indexing, for sensitive/dynamic sources. Self-serve disconnect removes indexed content.
numbers: 100+ prebuilt connectors; federated is read-only (writes from Oct 2026)
decision: Offer both modes per source behind one connector interface; policy decides which per customer.

title: Slack Real-Time Search API: query without storing
finding: RTS API lets third-party apps retrieve Slack data per query without storing customer data on external servers; MCP server GA on 2026-02-17.
decision: For Slack-like hostile-ToS sources, use the vendor's live search as the retrieval path and keep only pointers.

title: Dash ingest: metadata and content in index, plus dedupe
finding: On connect, metadata and content go to search and metadata stores after de-duplication, enrichment and content protections; knowledge graph built from content the user can access.
decision: Index-not-copy still stores derived text/embeddings: define exactly what (snippets, embeddings, metadata, ACL) and encrypt per tenant.

title: Embeddings are invertible
finding: Iterative correction recovers original text from dense embeddings.
decision: Treat embeddings as personal/confidential data: same residency, encryption, ACL and deletion as source text.

title: EDPB Opinion 28/2024 on AI models and personal data
finding: Anonymity of an AI model is judged case by case; authorities can order erasure of unlawfully processed data or even the model.
decision: Keep a source-to-derived lineage so a deletion can reach every embedding, snippet and cache entry.

title: Soft-deleted vectors may persist in indexes
finding: Argues derived embeddings are personal data and that soft-deleted HNSW entries can remain in raw index files; recommends redaction before embedding.
decision: Verify hard-delete by test: delete, compact, then probe; prefer per-tenant keys so crypto-shredding is possible.

title: Per-query live fetch (hydration) cost: tool definitions and results
finding: Tool definitions and intermediate results consume context; code execution and progressive tool disclosure keep bulk data out of the model.
decision: Hydrate in code outside the model, pass only the needed excerpt; load tool schemas on demand.

title: Federated retrieval limits (Dash on MCP)
finding: MCP tool definitions eat context and slow answers; mitigations: one super tool instead of 5-10 retrieval tools, store tool results outside the LLM context, sub-agents with narrow tool sets.
decision: Expose one retrieval tool to the model; fan out to connectors server-side.

title: Glean identity schema: sync users, groups, memberships
finding: Permissions are folded into one identity schema of groups/memberships and refreshed by periodic crawls because source permissions can change anytime.
numbers: Customers with hundreds of thousands of users; Salesforce identity crawl improved up to 98%
decision: Sync ACL and identity separately from content on its own (faster) schedule; filter stale/fake users.

title: Copilot connectors: ACL per item, permission-based filtering
finding: Every ingested item carries content, metadata and an ACL; search shows only items the user can access in the source.
decision: ACL travels with every chunk as metadata; query always carries the user identity.

title: Pre-filter vs post-filter for ACLs
finding: Consensus: put versioned ACL metadata on each chunk and filter inside the vector query; post-filtering leaks to the model and starves recall.
decision: Filter inside the index query; a stateless retriever that drops the user context must fail closed.

title: Live authorization check as the counterpoint
finding: Argues metadata filters suffer permission sync lag, huge group lists, and lose inheritance; recommends a real-time authz check on candidates before context reaches the model.
decision: Two-gate design: index pre-filter (coarse, fast) then live source check on the final top-N (authoritative).

title: MCP authorization: audience-bound tokens, no passthrough
finding: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE; RFC 8707 resource parameter; servers must validate audience and must not pass the client's token upstream.
numbers: PKCE S256 required; token in header not query string
decision: Use per-user, per-connector delegated tokens for live fetch; never forward one token across services.

title: Slack MCP server uses user tokens and scopes
finding: User-token OAuth, per-tool scopes, only directory-published or internal apps, admin approval, audit-log visibility.
decision: Live path inherits source permissions for free; prefer it where the vendor offers a permission-aware search endpoint.

title: Contextual retrieval: BM25 + embeddings + rerank
finding: Prepending chunk context then hybrid + rerank cuts top-20 retrieval failure.
numbers: Failure 5.7% -> 3.7% (-35%) -> 2.9% (-49% with BM25) -> 1.9% (-67% with rerank); $1.02 per million document tokens one-time; rerank 150 -> top 20
decision: Default pipeline: contextualized chunks, BM25 + dense, rerank top 150 to 20.

title: Small corpus: skip RAG
finding: If the knowledge base fits in context, put it all in the prompt (with caching).
decision: Rung 1 (tiny team) can skip the vector tier and use full-text plus long context.

title: Vespa hybrid ranking and RRF
finding: Text-match-required with vector ranking, weighted sums, or RRF; multi-phase ranking narrows candidates before expensive models.
numbers: Vendor claim: >100k QPS with ms latency (Berlin Buzzwords)
decision: Use RRF as a safe fusion default; add learned ranking only after an eval set exists.

title: Reranker quality and latency
source: Voyage via MongoDB blog + third-party latency
finding: Vendor claims rerank-2.5 beats Cohere v3.5; leaders are within 1-3 NDCG@10 on English per a third-party blog.
numbers: Rerank-2.5 +3.26% vs Cohere v3.5 (vendor); latency 80-150 ms (Cohere), 90-180 ms (2.5), 40-80 ms (lite) p50 (third-party)
decision: Budget ~100 ms for rerank; choose by own eval, not vendor tables.

title: Knowledge graph as index bundles, not a graph DB
finding: Graph DB had latency and query-pattern problems; Dash builds asynchronous knowledge bundles of cross-app relationships and indexes them with the normal pipeline.
decision: Entity layer = precomputed relationship bundles in the same index, not a separate graph store.

title: Glean knowledge graph per customer
finding: Per-customer graph of content, people and activity feeds ranking with semantic, keyword, freshness and personalization signals.
decision: Use people/activity signals as ranking features and for ACL expansion.

title: Agentic multi-step retrieval is token-expensive
finding: Orchestrator-worker multi-agent beat single agent on breadth research but costs far more tokens; token use explained most performance variance.
numbers: +90.2% vs single agent; agents ~4x chat tokens, multi-agent ~15x; tokens explain 80% of BrowseComp variance; simple fact 1 agent 3-10 tool calls
decision: Route: simple queries one-shot hybrid; agentic loop only for hard/broad questions with a hard token budget.

title: OpenAI file search: metadata filters and rate limits
finding: Hosted retrieval tool supports attribute filters; fewer results reduces tokens and latency.
decision: Keep retrieval behind our own gateway so a hosted tool is swappable, not a dependency.

title: Dash relevance eval with an LLM judge
finding: LLM judge on a 1-5 scale, improved with retrieval for acronyms and DSPy prompt optimization; scored with NDCG.
decision: Ship an LLM-judge plus human-labelled sample before tuning ranking.

title: turbopuffer published limits
finding: Namespace-per-tenant on object storage scales to very large tenants and tenant counts.
numbers: 1T+ docs / 3PB+ seen; 250M+ namespaces seen; 100k+ queries/s global; 5k+ q/s per namespace; 500M docs per shard; 256 shards/namespace; 10k writes/s per namespace; recall@10 90-100%
decision: Namespace per tenant (or per tenant-source) is the unit of isolation, sizing and deletion.

title: turbopuffer cold vs warm latency
finding: Object storage as source of truth with RAM/NVMe cache; centroid (SPFresh) index minimizes round trips.
numbers: Cold p50 874 ms and warm p50 14 ms at 1M docs; ~100 ms per storage round trip; strong consistency default, eventual up to ~1 h stale; write p50 165 ms for 500 kB; WAL 1 commit/s/namespace
decision: Design UX for a cold-tenant first query (~0.4-0.9 s) and pre-warm active tenants.

title: turbopuffer pricing
finding: Usage-based pricing dominated by writes for churny corpora.
numbers: Storage <=$0.33/GB-mo; writes <=$2.00/GB (10 KB min); queries <=$1.00/PB; Launch $16, Scale $256, Enterprise $4,096 /mo minimum
decision: ESTIMATE: 1M chunks x 1536 dims float32 = ~6.1 GB = ~$2/month storage at list rate; write only changed chunks (hash diff) to control the bill.

title: Pinecone serverless: blob store + freshness layer
finding: Writes commit to blob storage and a log; an index builder writes immutable segments; a freshness layer makes new/edited/deleted docs searchable in seconds; namespaces are hard isolation.
numbers: Gong costs 10x lower; avg latency -46.9%; cold start ~2 s typical, up to ~20 s at billions; design target hundreds of thousands of namespaces
decision: Adopt the log + immutable segments + freshness-layer pattern whichever engine is chosen.

title: Pinecone read-unit and storage pricing
finding: Query cost scales with namespace size, which rewards small per-tenant namespaces.
numbers: 1 RU per GB of namespace (min 0.25); fetch 1 RU per 10 records; storage $0.33/GB-mo; reads $16-18 per million (Standard)
decision: Many small namespaces keep per-query cost low; avoid one giant shared index.

title: Elastic BBQ quantization
finding: Binary quantization shrinks float32 vectors to bits with rerank on originals.
numbers: ~95% memory reduction; recall@10 0.84-0.95; up to 5x faster (3.9x avg) than OpenSearch FAISS on 2.5M x 1536-d (vendor benchmark)
decision: Quantize + oversample + rescore; keep full-precision vectors on cheap storage.

title: BBQ vs product quantization
finding: PQ can reach 32x reduction; Elastic claims BBQ matches recall and quantizes 10-50x faster.
decision: Quantization choice is an engine feature: do not hand-roll.

title: Notion: 10x scale, ~90% cost cut
finding: Moved from pod clusters to serverless, then to turbopuffer; per-page change detection; self-hosted embeddings.
numbers: Multi-billion objects; capacity 8x, active workspaces 15x; ~90% total cost cut; serverless -50%; turbopuffer -60% search spend, -35% EMR; p50 70-100 -> 50-70 ms; embeddings savings 90%+ is a projection
decision: Pay for usage not uptime; namespace per tenant removes custom sharding.

title: Notion: workspace-ID sharding and generations
finding: Start with workspace ID as partition key and range routing; generation IDs add shards without resharding; migrations reindex then cut over generation by generation.
decision: Include a generation field in routing from day 1 so embedding-model upgrades are cutovers, not outages.

title: Notion: per-span hashing avoids re-embedding
finding: 64-bit xxHash of span text and of metadata per span, one DynamoDB record per page; text change re-embeds that span, metadata change is a cheap PATCH.
decision: Content-hash every chunk; re-embed only on text change; ACL/metadata changes never re-embed.

title: Notion: two ingestion paths
finding: Offline Spark batch for onboarding/backfill, online Kafka consumers for live edits.
decision: Separate backfill lane from live lane so a big onboarding cannot delay fresh updates.

title: Notion: self-hosted embeddings on Ray
finding: Chunking and inference on one Ray compute layer; query embeddings on Ray Serve with dynamic batching; open models allow swapping models.
numbers: Removes a third-party API hop from the query path
decision: Own the embedding hop (or gateway) to cut latency and avoid model lock-in.

title: Glean connector pipeline: fetch, transform, push
finding: Custom connectors implement get_source_data, transform to a common document schema, and push via an uploader with batch/retry.
decision: One connector contract (fetch, map to common doc + ACL, push) so a new app is a mapping file plus auth.

title: Per-app queues because limits differ
finding: Each connector runs independently with its own queue because rate limits and data shapes differ.
decision: One queue and token bucket per (tenant, connector); one bad API cannot block others.

title: Connector effort at Dropbox: every app is a snowflake
finding: Custom crawlers per app; each has its own rate limit, API quirks and ACL model.
numbers: 50 open tabs and 50+ SaaS accounts per worker (context)
decision: Plan for per-app ACL adapters; keep the common schema thin (id, acl, text pointer, timestamps, type).

title: Microsoft: prebuilt plus custom connectors via a schema
finding: Custom connector = define schema, register app, write pull/push code; reserve custom work for unique sources.
decision: Ship prebuilt connectors for top apps, a schema-based SDK for the long tail.

title: MCP as universal live adapter
finding: Standard OAuth-based way for a client to call any compliant server on the user's behalf.
decision: Any app that ships an MCP server becomes a live-path connector with no custom crawler.

title: EchoLeak: prompt injection via retrieved email
finding: Zero-click exploit in Microsoft 365 Copilot chained classifier evasion, link-redaction bypass and an allowed proxy to exfiltrate data from a single crafted email.
numbers: CVE-2025-32711; CVSS 9.3; reported Jan 2025, fixed May 2025
decision: Treat all retrieved text as untrusted: strip active content, block auto-fetched URLs/images, no cross-scope data in one prompt.

title: Start eval with ~20 real queries
finding: Small early eval set from real usage is enough to see big effects; failure modes include duplicate work and hallucination on unusual queries.
decision: Seed eval with 20-50 real questions per tenant; add every reported bad answer.

title: Webhook loss and subscription expiry are normal
finding: Lifecycle notifications (subscriptionRemoved, reauthorizationRequired, missed) exist because events are lost.
numbers: Max delivery latency up to 6 h (driveItem)
decision: Freshness monitor: per-connector lag = now - last applied source timestamp; alert on a multiple of the connector SLA.

title: Delta replays and resets
finding: Same change can appear twice; 410 Gone demands restart.
decision: Idempotent apply keyed by (source id, version); weekly reconciliation scan to find drift.

title: Wrong-ACL and leak testing
finding: Retrieval service is a security boundary; test with adversarial and cross-tenant queries; a client without user context silently skips filters.
decision: Run a nightly canary: synthetic users must NOT retrieve planted forbidden docs; page on any hit.

title: Strong vs eventual consistency in the index
finding: Strong reads see their own writes; eventual reads are faster but can lag up to about an hour.
numbers: Eventual worst case ~1 h; strong WAL read ~10 ms
decision: Use strong reads for delete/ACL-revoke verification, eventual for ordinary queries.

title: Embedding model migration by re-index and cutover
finding: Full re-index with a newer model and gradual cutover, validating each generation.
decision: Keep old and new generations side by side until recall on the eval set passes.
